label: C1
title: The crooked needle
summary: Which unit-length rectifiable curve maximizes the chance of crossing at least one randomly placed ruled line?
statement: Let γ be any rectifiable plane curve of total length 1. Rotate γ uniformly through [0, π) and translate it by a uniformly random offset modulo 1 across parallel lines spaced 1 apart. The expected crossing count is 2/π, but the probability of at least one transverse crossing depends on γ. Which curve maximizes that probability, and what proof establishes optimality?
approach: Count crossings first: the integral-geometric mean is 2/π, so the gap between the mean count and the chance of any crossing is the room to optimize.

label: C2
title: The silent board
summary: Which Galton-board peg-removal patterns give exactly equal probability to every final bin?
statement: For each n ≥ 1, take n rows of a triangular Galton board, with states j = 0,…,r at row r = 0,…,n−1. A bead enters above row 0 at state j = 0. At site (r,j), an intact peg sends it to states j and j+1 with probability 1/2 each, independently; a removed peg sends it vertically to state j with probability 1. Classify every subset of removed sites for which the n+1 final-bin probabilities are exactly 1/(n+1), determine all n for which such a pattern exists, and prove the classification.
approach: Track each row as an exact rational distribution; a Julia search over every removal mask gives a small-n witness, while a proof must explain all n.

label: C3
title: The pile's memory
summary: What fraction of the identity sandpile on a 2n × 2n grid has height exactly two as n grows?
statement: Let Gₙ be the 2n × 2n square grid with open boundary, where each missing boundary edge leads to a sink, and let eₙ be the identity recurrent stable configuration of its abelian sandpile group, with heights 0, 1, 2, or 3. Define f(n) as the number of sites v with eₙ(v) = 2 divided by 4n². Prove that f(n) converges and find the limit, or give a rigorous numerical value to six digits with an explicit error bound.
approach: Use the burning test and the identity's recurrent structure, then compare exact finite grids with a provable finite-size bound.

label: C4
title: The butterfly's period
summary: At what first ρ does the Lorenz return map acquire a primitive orbit of period three?
statement: For the Lorenz system with σ = 10 and β = 8/3, let Σ = {(x,y,z) : x = 0, y > 0}, with the crossing direction fixed by ẋ > 0, and let Pρ be the first-return map on Σ. For ρ > 1, find the smallest ρ for which Pρ has a primitive period-three orbit, to six digits, and provide a verified enclosure of its three section points and connecting flow. Interval arithmetic or an equivalent proof-producing method must make the result rerunnable.
approach: Locate a primitive fixed point of Pρ³, then enclose all three section points and the intervening flow with interval arithmetic.

label: C5
title: The duelist's dice
problemType: Proof or exhaustive search with proof of exhaustiveness
summary: Can three fair six-sided dice form a non-transitive cycle with each win probability exactly two thirds?
statement: The cycle requires three fair six-sided dice A, B, and C. Each die has six pairwise-distinct positive integer faces; a face value may appear on a different die, and ties count as no win. Does a choice exist for which P(A > B) = P(B > C) = P(C > A) = 2/3? Give explicit face sets with the exact 36-pair counts, or prove that no such triple exists.
approach: Write each pairwise win count as an integer out of 36, use the required two-thirds count to constrain the face orderings, and make an exhaustive search independently checkable.
